The test image shows a corn leaf with large elongated tan/bleached streaks running parallel to veins, with orange/rust-colored flecks scattered within the bleached areas. Key features: elongated lesions, tan-gray coloring, orange flecks/freckles.

Top candidates: Goss's Wilt (tan streaks with bacterial freckles), Northern Leaf Blight (elongated tan lesions), Stewart's Disease (similar streak pattern).

The last reference (Goss's Wilt 126) shows very similar large elongated tan/bleached streaks running lengthwise on the leaf — this closely matches the test image pattern.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: large tan/bleached elongated streaks parallel to veins + scattered orange/rust flecks within the bleached areas
- Goss's Wilt reference matches: irregular tan lesions with bacterial exudate freckles (orange dots)
- NLB has distinct cigar-shaped lesions — not what's shown
- Stewart's Disease shows pale yellow streaks on seedlings — doesn't match
- The orange flecks within bleached areas are consistent with Goss's Wilt freckles (dried bacterial exudate), not rust pustules
